title: Trait base change of a Noetherian specialization with reduced closed fibre and two sections
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) between Noetherian schemes (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). Let $\sigma:T\to P$ be a section, $g\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_T$, and let $p\ne q$ be points of $P$ such that $p$ specializes to $q$. Schemes and sections are as in [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-section]. For a morphism $h:Y\to B$ with section $e$, set $C(h,e)=\{y\in Y\mid y\text{ belongs to the connected component of }e(h(y))\text{ in }h^{-1}(\{h(y)\})\}$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $q\in C(g,\sigma)$ and that the geometric fibre $P_{\overline{g(q)}}$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. There exist a discrete valuation ring $R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and a morphism $a:S=\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ taking the generic point $\eta$ to $p$ and the closed point $s$ to $q$. Put $b=g\circ a$, $X=P\times_TS$, and write $f:X\to S$, $r:X\to P$ for the projections [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\sigma_R:S\to X$ be the base-changed section and $\tau=(a,\mathrm{id}_S):S\to X$ the morphism determined by the projections. Then $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, $S$ and $X$ are Noetherian, and both the closed fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and its underlying topological space are Noetherian (for the space: every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes). Both $X_{\bar s}$ and $X_s$ are reduced. The maps $\sigma_R,\tau$ are sections of $f$, $r\circ\sigma_R=\sigma\circ b$, $r\circ\tau=a$, $r(\tau(\eta))=p$, and $r(\tau(s))=q$. Furthermore $C(f,\sigma_R)=r^{-1}C(g,\sigma)$, and $\tau(s)$ belongs to the connected component of $\sigma_R(s)$ in $f^{-1}(\{s\})$.

proof.text: Apply exists_trait_of_strict_specializes [lem-sbc-noetherian-specialization-trait] to obtain a DVR R and a morphism a with the prescribed generic and closed images. Put S = Spec R, b = a ≫ g, X = pullback g b, f = pullback.snd g b and r = pullback.fst g b. The closed point s satisfies b(s) = g(q).

Use stability under arbitrary base change to obtain Flat f, LocallyOfFinitePresentation f, QuasiCompact f and QuasiSeparated f. A DVR is a principal ideal ring and hence Noetherian; thus S is Noetherian. Local finite presentation implies local finite type by the existing Mathlib instance. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem makes X and its closed fibre Noetherian. Apply IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace directly to the latter.

Pullback pasting identifies the algebraic-closure base change of g.fiber(g(q)) with the geometric fibre appearing in hred. Transport reducedness across this isomorphism. Apply the arbitrary-field algebraic-closure criterion to obtain GeometricallyReduced for g.fiberToSpecResidueField(g(q)). The canonical square of ordinary fibres of the pullback square is cartesian, by Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback; since b(s)=g(q), base-change stability gives GeometricallyReduced for f.fiberToSpecResidueField(s). Over its residue field this morphism is flat and has reduced locally Noetherian base, so Mathlib GeometricallyReduced.isReduced_of_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian proves the ordinary closed fibre reduced. Apply geometric reducedness to the canonical algebraic closure of the residue field of s, and transport back along pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso to obtain exactly the asserted reduced geometric closed fibre. No change of chosen algebraic closure and no reduced-fibre-locus theorem are necessary.

Construct σR and τ with pullback.lift applied to (b ≫ σ, id) and (a, id). The lift projection equations prove both section equations and both first-projection equations. Evaluate τ ≫ r = a at the generic and closed points to obtain the required point images.

Apply section_component_preimage_of_isPullback [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] to the defining pullback square and the two projection equations of σR. Its symmetric equality is the desired component-locus equality. The equation r(τ(s))=q and hq put τ(s) in the inverse-image locus. Rewrite by that equality and use f(τ(s))=s to obtain membership in the connected component of σR(s) in the closed fibre.

proof_origin.place: Tag 055Q, second paragraph; Tags 054F and 055M. Reducedness is transported through the cartesian square of ordinary fibres using the arbitrary-field algebraic-closure criterion (Tags 035X and 020I) and Mathlib geometric-reducedness base-change API.
